title: Join two CPU tasks before returning
prompt: Split the vector at its middle. Launch two std::async tasks with std::launch::async, each returning its own long long subtotal. Wait for both and return their sum. Keep the borrowed vector alive until both finish. Tests check totals; review your code to verify that it uses two tasks and disjoint ranges.

tests.label: Odd length
tests.hint: The second range includes the remaining item.

tests.label: Wider accumulator
tests.hint: Accumulate in long long, not int.

hints: Each task should own its subtotal instead of sharing one writable total.
future.get waits for completion and retrieves the returned subtotal.
explanation: The tasks share only read access to the vector. Their totals are separate local values, and get establishes completion before the results are combined. Passing these fixtures does not prove a speedup or every concurrency property.
